answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, externally acquired token before it may post jobs or claim rewards. The protocol caps influence by locked value, not account count, and slashable deposits are forfeited when an identity double-claims or breaks an agreed task. Splitting funds across a timber, a vine, and a grove of aliases therefore creates no extra voting weight; the attacker must buy and lock more capital for longer, tying it up and risking loss.
